questions.question: Who among the following is a non-judicial member of the ﬁrst Lokpal of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 4) i.e.__ Archana Ramasundaram.__**

__
 
• Former first woman chief of Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB) **Archana Ramasundaram**__ was sworn in as a non-judicial member of Lokpal.
 
• President Ram Nath Kovind administered the oath of office to **Justice Pinaki Chandra Ghose **as the country's first Lokpal.
 
• Former Chief Justices of different high courts - Justices **Dilip B Bhosale**, **Pradip Kumar Mohanty**, **Abhilasha Kumari **and** Ajay Kumar Tripathi** - took oath as judicial members in the Lokpal.

questions.question: The grasshopper has its ears located near ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** option 2) i.e. __Legs.__**

 
• The hearing organ, which is a large membrane called a **tympanum**, is located on either side of the first segment of the abdomen, near the base of the** hind legs**.
 
• The grasshoppers have three main body parts – **the head, the thorax and the abdomen**.
 
• They have **six jointed legs, two pairs of wings and two antennae**.
 
• Their body is covered with a hard exoskeleton.
 
• Grasshoppers breathe through a series of holes called ‘**spiracles**’ which are located along the sides of the body.
 
• Most grasshoppers are green, brown, or olive-green.
 
• The biggest Grasshoppers are about 11.5 centimetres long.
 
• Their legs are long hind legs that are used for hopping and jumping and the short front legs are used to hold prey and to walk.

questions.question: Khichdi, Uttarayan and Lohri are different names of the festival _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 1) i.e. __Makar Sankranti__.**

__
 
• **Makar Sankranti**__ is celebrated in various parts of India to observe the day which marks the shift of the sun into ever-lengthening days.
 
• It also marks the beginning of the **end of Winter **and the **harvest of rabi crops.**
 
• While __**Makar Sankranti**__ is most popular in West India, down south, the festival is known as** Pongal** and in the north, it is celebrated as **Lohri**.
 
• **Uttarayan, Maghi, Khichdi** are some other names of the same festival.
 
• It falls on the same date in the local calendar every year on **January 14.**
